title: Resting long ants, take two: the clock was the bug
question: Same three candidates, now actually reaching the long-bodied ants. Does any of them read as resting rather than stuck? off is today's shipped look.
context_md:
**Your verdict on the first card, verbatim:** *"The creatures that I think look stuck are stuck in all of them. Although this is a very short gif to have to judge this on."*

Both halves of that turned out to be right, for a reason worth naming plainly: **the first card was built on a real bug, and it mostly did not fire on the ants you were looking at.**

`IDLE_ANIM_DELAY` (how long an animal has to hold still before it starts animating) was counted in *render calls*, not in world ticks. The capture tool samples one render call per 10 world ticks, so the 60-render-frame delay was actually costing **600 world ticks** -- 40% of the first card's 1,500-tick window gone before any animal could be flagged at all. Measured directly (a new probe drives the real scenario and counts): only **8 of 22** full-length long ants ever animated in that window. Fixed to count world ticks, the same window gives **21 of 22**. That is almost certainly why the fix looked like it was doing nothing to the animals you pointed at -- it mostly wasn't running on them.

**This card is the corrected mechanism, and it is also 4x longer** (6,000 ticks against 1,500, same `every=` sampling density so the frame count is the same), because your second point was also a real finding and not a side note: a resting ant's idle streaks run tens of thousands of frames, and a short clip can show neither a cycling animation nor the thing it's meant to contrast with -- a body that has genuinely not moved in 50,000 frames. Same scene as before (`played_bed_longant`, seed 3, same crop/zoom you already marked: `zoom=4 crop=160,120,224,56`), starting at the same frame 28,000, running to 34,000.

**I do not yet have your three markers from the first card** (the sync hadn't landed when I started this pass), so this can't yet confirm whether the *specific* ants you pointed at are among the ones now animating, or whether they're in the `moving`/`crossing`/`flight` states this doesn't touch -- or whether they're just as stuck as ever. If they still read as stuck once you've had a real look at this, that's `open-bugs-handoff.md` §Z13's explanation (c): the three-ant sample it was built on missed a real movement failure, and the fix belongs in the walk, not the look. That's cheap to check once I have the coordinates.

`head`/`antennae`/`shuffle` are unchanged in concept from the first card (a brightness pulse, a bright tick past the head, a one-cell reach) -- only the timing base under all three was wrong.
